properties.evidence: Corroboration rather than conflict, and the pair is the general shape: BOTH say a branch-local green says nothing about the merge base. The older fact measured it on the LOCAL gate (HEAD vs HEAD~1, so a stacked branch has no merge base to check against); this one measures the same blindness one level up, where the branch is internally coherent and the SUBTRACTION against main is what nothing checks. 2026-08-16 added a third instance on the same theme: #194's base branch was another PR's branch rather than main, so its green CI had been testing the wrong base entirely, `gh` reported MERGEABLE until that base was merged and deleted, and retargeting the base to main did NOT re-trigger CI — a force-push was needed. `SUPPLEMENTS` would be the better word; no edge type models TemporalFact to TemporalFact, so this uses the corroboration form rather than asserting a relation the schema does not carry.
